shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical description of a mobile, submucosal mass

shortlist.label: Ectopic lymph node
shortlist.why_kept: Considered in differential diagnosis based on clinical and radiographic findings

shortlist.label: Mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a swelling in the cheek with a smooth mucosal surface

shortlist.label: Sialadenitis
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the severe pain and swelling in the cheek region

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common salivary gland tumor that could present as a submucosal mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a solitary, mobile, submucosal mass with a smooth mucosal surface and a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion on ultrasonography is consistent with a lipoma, which is a common benign tumor composed of fat tissue.

rejected.label: Ectopic lymph node
rejected.why: Ectopic lymph nodes are rare in the oral cavity and would not typically present as a mobile, submucosal mass.

rejected.label: Mucocele
rejected.why: Mucoceles are typically associated with a history of trauma or blockage of a salivary gland duct, and would not typically present as a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion on ultrasonography.

rejected.label: Sialadenitis
rejected.why: Sialadenitis is inflammation of the salivary gland, which would typically present with signs of infection such as redness, warmth, and swelling, rather than a solitary, mobile mass.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: Pleomorphic adenoma is a type of salivary gland tumor that would typically present as a slow-growing, painless mass, rather than a rapidly growing, painful mass as described in the vignette.
